title: North African Urfa Lamb Merguez Logs
displayTitle: North African Urfa Lamb Merguez Logs
seoTitle: North African Urfa Lamb Merguez Logs | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Merguez night—bold lamb spice, fast char, skewers that survive a hold
subtitle: Urfa-spiced lamb logs, preserved lemon yogurt, and char for ten
description: Ground lamb mixes with urfa pepper, fennel, and ras el hanout, forms around flat skewers, and grills until charred and 165°F. Serve with preserved-lemon yogurt and grilled naan.

steps.title: Mix merguez lamb
steps.instruction: Combine lamb, urfa biber, fennel, ras el hanout, cinnamon, drained shallot, and salt until uniform. Mix until tacky, about 3 minutes.

steps.title: Form skewer logs
steps.instruction: Press lamb around wide flat skewers in 8-inch logs about 1 inch thick. Chill 30 minutes on a sheet pan. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Build preserved-lemon yogurt
steps.instruction: Whisk yogurt with minced preserved lemon rind and pinch of salt. Keep cold until service. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium-high, 425°F. Oil grates—lamb fat will flare; keep a cooler zone ready. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill merguez skewers
steps.instruction: Grill skewers 4–5 minutes per side until deeply charred and 160°F internal. Move to indirect heat if flare-ups hit. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 5 minutes to 165°F carryover. Slide onto hotel pans, cover with foil, hold at 170°F until service. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Warm flatbread
steps.instruction: Wrap flatbread in foil bundles and warm on the grill 2–3 minutes at 400°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tonight's line
steps.instruction: Serve two skewers per firefighter with harissa yogurt and flatbread. Call temps: pull at 165°F, held at 170°F max. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Wide flat skewers keep ground lamb from spinning on the grill.
Chill formed logs—they hold shape better over direct heat.
Harissa yogurt stays cold on the side so skewers hold without curdling sauce.
tonightSpread: Merguez skewers with harissa yogurt and warm flatbread.
leftovers: Crumble lamb into pita with extra harissa yogurt.
Chop into couscous with preserved lemon.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Merguez brings lamb variety beyond kofta or harissa chicken. Skewers cook in minutes between calls and hold covered at 170°F without drying if pulled at temp.
mealPrepNotes: Chill formed skewers 30 minutes. Grill medium-high 425°F. Hold finished skewers covered at 170°F up to 30 minutes—do not exceed 175°F or lamb toughens. Calls: pull at 165°F, rest 5 minutes before sliding off.
